summary: FloodSense-PK is a flood intelligence and early-warning dashboard for Pakistan. During monsoon floods, clouds block optical satellites, so we use Sentinel-1 radar with a U-Net (ResNet34) deep learning model to map floodwater through clouds and at night. We compare current flooding against the 2010 Great Pakistan Floods, reconstructed from NASA/USGS Landsat 5 imagery using the MNDWI water index, to produce a “Delta Severity” score showing whether today’s flooding is worse or better than 2010. NASA SRTM elevation data removes steep-terrain false positives. We also pull live river discharge from Pakistan’s Flood Forecasting Division and combine all three signals into a 1-10 risk score and an AI-generated tactical briefing for disaster managers. It works at district, province, and national scale and helps authorities decide where to send relief first.
details:
What it does: FloodSense-PK fuses three evidence streams:

(1) NOW: Sentinel-1 SAR processed by a U-Net ResNet34 model (trained on Sen1Floods11, validation IoU 0.55) to map current floodwater;

(2) THEN: a 2010 flood baseline built from NASA/USGS Landsat 5 TM imagery using MNDWI, with 2009 permanent water removed;

(3) LIVE: river discharge and status scraped from Pakistan’s Flood Forecasting Division. These combine into a weighted 1-10 risk score (40% flood extent, 30% change vs 2010, 30% hydraulic status) and a structured AI tactical report.

How it works: Google Earth Engine retrieves the Sentinel-1 composite and Landsat 5 data. NASA SRTM elevation is used to mask slopes above 15° to reduce terrain false positives. Large SAR tiles are split into 256×256 patches, run through the model, and stitched into a flood mask with a probability map and affected area in km². A Streamlit dashboard presents Overview, Detection, River Flows, and AI Intelligence tabs, with analysis at district, province, or national scale.

Impact: Disaster authorities get a fast, cloud-independent view of where flooding is worst and how it compares with the 2010 disaster, supporting decisions on evacuation and relief.

Tools: Python, PyTorch, segmentation-models-pytorch, Google Earth Engine, Streamlit, Pydeck, GeoPandas, Rasterio.

Limitations (honest): VH is approximated from VV at inference; the model was trained on global data and not yet fine-tuned or validated on Pakistan-specific floods; 2010 optical vs current SAR is a benchmark indicator, not a pixel-exact difference.

Creativity: The 2010 “Delta Severity” benchmark gives raw flood percentages an intuitive meaning for non-technical decision makers.
dataRefs: Landsat 5 TM Collection 2 Level 2 (USGS/NASA Landsat program)
projectRefs: Pakistan Flood Forecasting Division River State
